assign.tab: Layout browser and design - monorepo - Visual Studio Code
assign.request: Improve the mastermind's first cut of the v2 AI dashboard at /framework/ai/v/2/: newest-run auto-pick, a compact/cozy/roomy density switch on the design system's --size knob with no text under 12px, reclaim the empty top/side space, fix topics losing their heading across columns, dismissible notes, a decisions panel reusing ext/AITask/decisions.js's verdict writer, measure the live append-to-DOM delay, a small readme.
assign.now: reading the mastermind's first cut and the design system's size standard
steps: read the v2 board and the size standard
shoot 400/1280/1920/3440 x3 densities, fix on second look

log.msg: usage.json refresh skipped — public/framework/ai/usage.json is outside this task's fence (only public/framework/ai/v/** and this task dir); the mastermind keeps the snapshot current. Read directly: session 9% used, week 30% used.

assign.now: measured the mastermind's cut live, then rewrote page.js + v2.css in place

decision.about: how the board finds the run to show

options.say: newest task dir whose slug starts mastermind-, from directory.json alone
options.why: zero extra fetches, matches the real live run today

options.say: fetch every task's task.jsonl across every day and read its group field
options.why: catches a task that never uses the mastermind- naming habit

options.say: slug scan first (free); if nothing matches anywhere, fetch and check group:"ai-ops" for TODAY's tasks only
options.why: both signals work, cost never grows with the archive

decision.because: the slug scan alone already finds the real run with no network cost; the group check is real, not just documented, but bounded to today so a month of history is never scanned to answer one page load.

decision.about: how compact/cozy/roomy should scale the board

options.say: a board-only --v2-size custom property, independent of the site's --size
options.why: no risk of colliding with framework.css's own control scaling

options.say: literally .size-small/.size-regular/.size-large (framework.css), with max(12px, ...) floors on every font-size this file declares
options.why: the owner's own instruction: use the design system's knob, do not invent one

decision.because: framework.css already ships exactly this ladder (0.75/1/1.5); reusing it means a future site-wide size change reaches this board for free. The floor had to be added explicitly because reusing --size also fed framework's own control rule (button/textarea font-size: calc(1em*var(--size))) a second time, which pushed a Send button to 9px before max(12px, ...) landed on every declaration.

decision.about: how to close the ~83px top / ~66px side gap around the board

options.say: classes: "full" on this page's own Page config (the old .page.full alias, --gutter-x/--pad-y: 0)
options.why: a one-line config change, no new CSS

options.say: in v2.css: .page:has(> .page-catalog .v2) { --gutter-x: 0; --pad-y: 0 } — zeroing the OUTER ai/ catalog page's own tokens only while this board is the mounted leaf
options.why: the gap measured as coming from the catalog's own wide-track inset (ext/catalog/catalog.js: every catalog child is inset, by design), one level up from this page

decision.because: measured live: classes:"full" changes tokens on THIS page's own grid, which the catalog wide-track placement sits outside of — it left the gap untouched. The outer page's own tokens were the real cause; :has() re-evaluates with the route so only this board is affected. Measured 1920: 83px top / 66px sides before, 35px top / 0px sides after (top later fell further once density's own padding shrank too).

decision.about: topics losing their heading across CSS columns

options.say: keep a topic whole when short; a long one splits with a repeated "(continued)" head
options.why: keeps the dense multi-column reading flow the first cut had

options.say: switch .v2-asks from CSS `columns` to a grid of topic CARDS (grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(24em,100%),1fr)))
options.why: a grid item cannot be split across a track — the heading can never separate from its own rows

decision.because: CSS columns cannot insert a repeated head at an arbitrary break point without JS measuring where the browser chose to break, which is exactly the kind of machinery the brief asked to avoid; a grid guarantees the invariant structurally. Traded for uneven column heights (no masonry packing here) — looked fine at 1280/1920/3440 in the shot.

decision.about: where the reused Decisions panel goes

options.say: a fourth panel alongside From the mastermind / In flight / Needs you, in the same row
options.why: matches the brief's first-listed option, keeps the top row as one unit

options.say: its own full-width row below, collapsed to one summary line by default, opening on click
options.why: a topic of their own, per the brief's second option

decision.because: measured: 14 real decisions (each can open its own reply box) in a 20em column made the WHOLE top row as tall as the decisions list, pushing firstAskY from 602px to 2338px at 1920 — asks, the board's main job, fell off the first screen entirely. Full width fixed the height fight; folding it shut by default (open count still shown) keeps the first screen about asks, per CLAUDE.md's own presentation rule that detail nests one click down.

log.msg: Live delay measured for real: 3 note appends to the run's own task.jsonl (msg says "test", ids prefixed v2-delay-test-), file-write to DOM text, same Node clock both ends, real dev socket on the private :8135 server. Results: 14.8ms, 11.1ms, 13.3ms — median 13.3ms.

Before -> after at 1920, compact density: board top 83px -> 23px; empty side gutter 66.5px each side -> 0px; first ask's y 602px -> ~608px (about the same, now paying for the run label + density switch + a one-line Decisions fold, which is a net new feature); asks visible on first screen 70 -> ~61 (viewport-height dependent, both runs read against the live, still-growing log); smallest font 12px -> 12px at compact and cozy (the floor binds), 18px at roomy (does not need to).

No console errors and no horizontal scrollbar at 400/1280/1920/3440, all three densities (12 shots) - proof.mjs in the scratchpad. Interactive smoke test (interact.mjs): density click updates the class and Page.Store; dismissing a note removes its row and remembers the id; the Decisions fold opens the real ext/AITask/decisions.js rows and closes again - all headless, no Approve/Improve/Send clicked (those write a real verdict/rank line to the live run log, out of fence).

assign.outcome: **The v2 board finds its own run, breathes to a density you pick, and keeps every topic's heading.** [The board](/framework/ai/v/2/) — before: fixed run, one fixed size, the top/side gutter empty, a topic's rows split silently across a column break. After: the newest `mastermind-` run auto-picked (`?run=` overrides, a fallback constant underneath); a Compact/Cozy/Roomy switch on the design system's own `--size` knob, remembered per browser, with `max(12px, …)` on every font-size so no setting can go under 12px; the catalog's own top/side inset zeroed just for this board (83px top / 66px each side -> 23px / 0px at 1920, compact); topics as a card grid instead of CSS columns, so a heading can never separate from its own rows; notes with a dismiss x (the line stays in the log) and an "earlier" fold; landed agents show their real first sentence, not a throwaway "Landed."; a Decisions panel that calls ext/AITask/decisions.js's real Approve/Improve/rank writer, full width, folded to one line by default so it does not push the asks off the first screen. Live delay measured for real (3 file-writes to the run's own log, socket to DOM text, same clock both ends): 14.8ms, 11.1ms, 13.3ms, median 13.3ms. [readme.md](/framework/ai/v/2/readme.md) says the shape; the `note` verb is now one line in new-task's own verb list and a proposal line in the mastermind skill's improvements.md. Left: no true masonry packing for uneven topic-card heights (the CSS `masonry` value isn't shipping yet, and a JS packer felt like more machinery than a dashboard needs) — noted in the readme as the accepted tradeoff for never losing a heading.
